_how_to_edit: Each item needs a unique id (lowercase, dashes). 'for' can include recovery, together, healing. 'url' and 'by' are optional. Keep the commas and quotes exactly as they are.

sections.title: Find support
sections.intro: Recovery is easier with other people. These groups are free or low cost, and many meet online.

items.title: Sex Addiction group sessions on BetterHelp
items.text: Many of the resources on this site were first shared in these group sessions. You need a BetterHelp membership to join. This site isn't affiliated with BetterHelp or the group.

items.title: Sex Addicts Anonymous (SAA)
items.text: Free 12-step fellowship for people who want to stop compulsive sexual behavior. Meetings in person, by phone, and online.

items.title: Sex and Love Addicts Anonymous (SLAA)
items.text: Free 12-step group that also covers love and relationship addiction.

items.title: S-Anon
items.text: Free 12-step fellowship for partners, family, and friends hurt by someone else's sexual behavior. Meetings around the world, plus phone support.

items.title: COSA
items.text: Free 12-step fellowship for people whose lives have been affected by someone else's compulsive sexual behavior.

items.title: Recovering Couples Anonymous (RCA)
items.text: Free 12-step fellowship for couples who want to rebuild commitment, communication, and caring together.

sections.title: Recovery practices
sections.intro: Ideas that come up again and again in recovery groups.

items.title: Bring the session home
items.text: For partners: ask your partner to go to their group, take notes, and share them with you after.

points.text: You get to see what they're learning.
It's an easy way for them to practice being open with you.
It gives you both something to talk about besides the hurt.
When you're with your partner, don't be preoccupied. Limit sitting on the couch on your phones. Pay attention, because they've probably already told you what they need to trust you.
Stop the little lies, and be open even when it might not go well.
Trust comes back on your partner's schedule, not yours.
If certain places or people trigger you, plan ahead so you stay safe.
Call your partner, a friend, or family. You don't have to share details. Talk about the trigger or anything else to get your mind off it.
Ask yourself if you're hungry, angry, lonely, or tired, and take care of that first.
Urges pass. Give it 15 minutes and go for a walk.

items.title: Natural ways to help your mood
items.text: Sunlight, exercise, healthy food, yoga, sleep, probiotics, and omega-3s.

items.title: Medication: talk to your doctor
items.text: Medication helps some people with compulsive behavior. Talk to your doctor about whether it's right for you.

items.title: Out of the Shadows
items.text: Usually the first book people get recommended. A lot of how sex addiction is treated today comes from this book.

items.title: Facing the Shadow
items.text: The workbook that goes with Out of the Shadows. Good for your first steps in recovery.

items.title: A Gentle Path Through the Twelve Steps
items.text: A workbook for the 12 steps. Less rigid and more reflective.

items.title: Sex Addicts Anonymous ("The Green Book")
items.text: SAA's main book. A must if you're working the SAA program.

items.title: Don't Call It Love
items.text: Carnes's research on people with sex addiction. Helpful for seeing yourself in the patterns.

items.title: Contrary to Love
items.text: About helping someone with sex addiction. Partners and therapists read this one a lot.

items.title: In the Shadows of the Net
items.by: Patrick Carnes, David Delmonico & Elizabeth Griffin
items.text: About compulsive online sexual behavior. Good if most of your acting out happens on screens.

items.title: Out of the Doghouse
items.text: A step-by-step guide for fixing the relationship after you've been caught.

items.title: Help Her Heal
items.by: Carol Juergensen Sheets & Vicki Tidwell Palmer
items.text: An empathy workbook to help your partner heal. You can do it alone or together.

items.title: Sex, Lies, and the Other Woman
items.text: For the betrayed partner. Helps with the "why did this happen?" question.

items.title: The Porn Trap
items.text: A guide to spotting and recovering from porn problems. Good for individuals and couples.

items.title: Mind Over Explicit Matter
items.text: How porn changes the brain and how to undo it.

items.title: Every Man's Battle
items.text: A Christian book on sexual purity and self-control. Very common in faith-based recovery.

items.title: Dopamine Nation
items.text: A Stanford psychiatrist on how modern life overloads the brain and what to do about it. Goes well with The Molecule of More.

items.title: The Molecule of More
items.by: Daniel Z. Lieberman & Michael E. Long
items.text: All about dopamine and why your brain craves what it craves.

items.title: The Power of Habit
items.text: How habits form and how to change them. Useful for replacing acting out with something better.

items.title: No Bad Parts
items.text: An intro to Internal Family Systems (IFS) therapy. Helps with deep beliefs you have about yourself.

items.title: Attachment Theory Workbook for Couples
items.text: Exercises to figure out your attachment styles and why you connect the way you do.

items.title: The Presence Process
items.text: A 10-week practice for staying in the moment. Helps with the "be where your feet are" part of recovery.

items.title: Good Vibes, Good Life
items.text: About self-love as the starting point for change. More mindset than clinical.

items.title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
items.text: About choosing what's actually worth your energy. Blunt but helpful.

items.title: Porn, Betrayal, Sex and the Experts (PBSE)
items.text: Two therapists who are in recovery themselves answer questions from addicts, partners, and couples. Really good on disclosure and rebuilding trust.

items.title: Dare to Connect
items.text: The PBSE hosts' live online program, with sessions for addicts, spouses, and couples.

items.title: Unhooked
items.text: What porn does to your brain and body, plus a mindfulness approach to quitting.

items.title: Unravelling the Big Mystery
items.text: The psychology behind porn addiction. A good place to start if you want to understand the why.

items.title: Solved: How to Let Go of Your Shame
items.text: A deep dive into shame and how it feeds addiction. It's a longer listen.

items.title: Dr. Trish Leigh
items.text: A brain coach who makes short videos about porn recovery and what's going on in your brain.

items.title: Joy Recovery
items.text: Roy and Jacqueline are a husband and wife who are certified recovery coaches. They've been through infidelity and betrayal trauma themselves and work with individuals and couples.

items.title: The Anatomy of Trust
items.text: Brené Brown breaks trust into seven parts called BRAVING: Boundaries, Reliability, Accountability, Vault, Integrity, Nonjudgment, and Generosity. Trust gets built in small, everyday moments.

sections.title: Apps and accountability tools
sections.intro: Apps can help, but they don't replace doing the work. Check each site for current prices.

items.title: Covenant Eyes
items.text: The most popular accountability app. Your partner gets an easy-to-read report of anything flagged. Faith-based.

items.title: Ever Accountable
items.text: Sends weekly reports to up to three accountability partners. Usually cheaper than Covenant Eyes.

items.title: Canopy
items.text: Blocks explicit content before it loads. Your partner can stop it from being uninstalled.

items.title: Truple
items.text: Takes random screenshots and sends them to an accountability partner. It monitors instead of blocking. Works best on Android.

items.title: AppBlock
items.text: Lets you block risky apps and websites.

items.title: Brick
items.text: A physical device that locks the apps you pick until you tap your phone on it again. One-time cost, no subscription. Works best if someone else holds onto it.

items.title: Unchaind
items.text: A Christian app with streak tracking, daily check-ins, and scripture. Needs a subscription.

items.title: Quitter
items.text: Tracks your streak and shows how your brain is recovering. A few apps use this name, so check the reviews before you download.
